result.title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases and exceed ordinary repeated-generation variability. Probability canonicalization substantially reduces framing sensitivity, identifying probability representation as a practical target for improving consistency in high-stakes LLM decision support.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 FrameBench-HPS 基准（240 个高风险场景、2880 条提示），在七个 LLM 上检验同一概率以收益/损失框架表述时建议是否改变，并发现概率规范化能显著降低框架敏感性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「等价概率、不同输出」的现象为 LVR 中任务必要信息能否在内部状态被一致保留提供可核查线索，概率规范化与不变性评价或可类比到置信表示与停止决策，但跨模态可迁移性需核查。
